newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end easier, despite Roche gain.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end easier, despite Roche gain.

text.p: Swiss share prices ended slightly lower despite the fact that Roche certificates, the most actively traded stock, posted a 1.4 percent gain.
Prices came under pressure in late trade from a weaker Wall Street opening. Robust U.S. consumer confidence data, which hit a 28-year high, raised fears of higher interest rates, dealers said.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended down 6.7 points, or 0.13 percent, at 5,190.0. The broad SPI ended off 3.40 points at 3,281.28.
Certificates of Roche, which on Monday announced plans to buy German Boehringer Mannheim for some $11 billion, ended 190 francs higher at 13,195, off a day's high of 13,300.
The stock clawed back Monday's losses, which came after Roche said the purchase of Boehringer would lead to a significant dilution of earnings in the first year.
In early trade the certificates had fallen as far as 12,820 francs, but rebounded after the market took a more favourable view of the Boehringer acquisition, one trader said.
Novartis registered shares closed five francs lower at 1,995.

Ciba SC, Monday's clear winner among blue chips, slumped 10.25 francs to 141.50. Traders said the price swings of recent sessions probably stemmed from position adjustments ahead of the company's first quarter results which are expected Wednesday before the bourse opens.
Financials were more under pressure than industrials. Banks CS Group, SBC, and insurers Winterthur and Baloise were off more than one percent each. UBS bearers rose three francs to 1,550.
Second-tier Fischer was up 50 to 1,984, profiting from a higher profit estimate by a Zurich private bank.
